solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Voguish point of view taken for example

parts.note: something voguish is fashionable, or in
a stance is a position or attitude on a question

explanation.surface: A trendy opinion offered up as a model case.
explanation.definitionFit: A case or illustration of something is an example of it, as in the phrase for instance.

clue.text: On plane, transporting grand sort of printer

indicators.note: transporting means carrying, so the plane and on carry the grand within them

parts.note: on can mean in, as in on the team or in the team
a jet is a jet-propelled aeroplane
K is slang for a thousand, a grand

explanation.surface: Someone on an aircraft carrying a piano, of some kind of printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like a piano or an adjective; it is the slang for a thousand, shortened to K.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkjet is a common type of printer that sprays tiny drops of ink onto paper.

clue.text: Invertebrate chicken?

definitions.meaning: an invertebrate creature has no backbone
chicken as an adjective means cowardly, lacking backbone

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a backbone describes both an animal without vertebrae and a person without courage.

clue.text: A permit held in the jumper perhaps

indicators.note: held in says the permit sits inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written
to let is to permit or allow

explanation.surface: A licence kept in a sweater, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a sweater, a British word for a pullover; here it is a high jumper or long jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumper in track and field is one kind of sportsperson, hence the question mark style perhaps.

clue.text: Influence strike

definitions.meaning: influence here means power or weight in affairs
strike here means a hit or blow

explanation.definitionFit: Clout means both political pull and a heavy blow with the hand.

clue.text: Thrash to attend in university

parts.note: to attend somewhere is to be at it
a student at university is said to be up, in British usage

explanation.surface: To be beaten for going to college.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is British usage, as at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat up someone is to thrash them, a phrasal verb for a violent assault.

clue.text: Yours truly in the grip of uncontrollable greed, as became apparent

indicators.note: in the grip of says one piece is held inside another
uncontrollable says the letters of greed run wild into a new order

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me, the speaker

explanation.surface: The writer, caught by wild avarice, came to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncontrollable' makes ERGED from greed; ME goes in after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that emerged came out into view, so it became apparent.

clue.text: Horrible being right in the grip of tax

indicators.note: in the grip of says right is held inside the tax

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Something nasty that properly sits inside a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is an ugly monster of Scandinavian folklore, a horrible creature.

clue.text: A tidy pro's sporting way to eliminate foot faults

indicators.note: sporting is read as showing off or rearranging, so these letters change order

parts.note: taken as written
the possessive is ignored, leaving the word pro

explanation.surface: A neat professional's tennis method for stopping foot faults on serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot faults' is a tennis term about serving; here it means problems with feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiropody, the treatment of feet, is a way of curing their defects.

clue.text: Shocked the beginning came first!

parts.note: a start is the beginning
led means came first or was in front

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how the start was at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be startled is to be given a sudden fright, a synonym for shocked.

clue.text: Tramp, dubbed as this wandering king, to head forth

indicators.note: wandering says the letters roam into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vagrant knighted as a roving monarch setting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubbed as this' is a nod to knights being dubbed; the anagram uses only 'king, to head forth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Knight of the road is a humorous phrase for a vagrant or hobo who roams the highways.

clue.text: Ingredient section of clientele mentioned

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A part of the customers that got a mention.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component or constituent, one of the things that make something up.

clue.text: Beer overturned by one with a princely habit

indicators.note: overturned says the beer is turned upside down, read backwards in a down light sense

parts.note: lager is a kind of beer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pint knocked over by someone with a lordly custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' looks like a custom but means dress, as a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the robes and emblems of royalty, so the clothing of a prince.

clue.text: Set out, cycle round base

indicators.note: round says the cycling goes around the other letters

parts.note: to pedal is to cycle

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Get going, ride a bike around the base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycle' looks like a noun for a bike or a series; here it is the verb meaning to ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base or support on which a column or statue stands.

clue.text: Attempt to involve an undergarment — that's distortion

indicators.note: to involve means to include, so the attempt wraps around the garment

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an gives the letter A
a vest is an undergarment, in Britain worn under a shirt

explanation.surface: Trying to incorporate underwear makes a mockery of things.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque distortion or parody of something.

clue.text: Submit to delay

definitions.meaning: submit means yield, as in ... to someone's judgement
delay means put off or postpone

explanation.definitionFit: Defer means both yielding to another and postponing a decision.

clue.text: Fancy-free member and miss, embracing love

parts.note: the foot is a member, a limb

indicators.note: embracing says the miss hugs the love inside it

parts.note: to lose is to miss, as with a train
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A carefree limb and a girl, cuddling her darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' reads as a young woman but is the verb lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Being footloose means free of ties, carefree, able to go anywhere.

clue.text: Loyal woman developed flu

parts.note: Faith is a woman's name

indicators.note: developed means changed or turned into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trusty lady came down with the flu.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithful means steadfast and true, synonymous with loyal.

clue.text: Salvation Army, looking back, established something worth having

indicators.note: looking back says the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: set means established or fixed

explanation.surface: The charity, reflecting, founded something valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something of value, a benefit or resource worth having.

clue.text: Pedal with lad playing in bay, maybe

indicators.note: in says the scrambled lad goes inside the tree

parts.note: the bay is one kind of tree, the laurel

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played around with, giving a new order

explanation.surface: A pedal pushed by a boy frolicking at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' suggests the coast, but it is the bay laurel, an example of a tree, hence 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a lever worked by the foot, as on an old sewing machine.

clue.text: Attachment or obsession, getting caught out

indicators.note: getting out says a letter is removed from the obsession
getting out says a letter is removed from the obsession

parts.note: an addiction is an obsession or compulsion
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Fondness or fixation leading to being found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'out' frame 'caught': take C from ADDICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition is something attached or added on, as an annex is to a building.

clue.text: Poles seen in property — items can't be delivered while they're in it

definitions.text: items can't be delivered while they're in it

indicators.note: seen in says the poles appear inside the property

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic or property
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Explorers in a building, and goods stuck in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods in transit are on the way and so not yet delivered.

clue.text: Ravel's given me shivers, in one section

indicators.note: in one section says the answer lies in one stretch of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A composer's work gives me the shivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the French composer, but it is the verb meaning entangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle or entwine, just as to enmesh is to catch in a net.

clue.text: Acrobat's appliance of skill, flipping vegetables, we hear

indicators.note: flipping says the skill is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

indicators.note: we hear says the vegetables are sounded out, not spelt

parts.note: peas are vegetables

explanation.surface: A circus device of craft, with vegetables tossed about by name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns ART into TRA; PEAS said aloud gives PEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is the swinging bar from which acrobats perform.

clue.text: One's passed by majority

parts.note: majority here is the legal coming of age at eighteen, not most of the votes in an election

explanation.definitionFit: Someone grown up has reached the age of majority, the legal age of maturity.

clue.text: Clergyman drops a vintage comic?

indicators.note: drops says a letter is let fall from the word

parts.note: a chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution

explanation.surface: A priest loses an old cartoon book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' looks like a magazine, but means a comedian: Charlie Chaplin of silent films.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was a silent-film comedian, so a comic from a bygone era.

clue.text: Companion harvested corn and last of hay

indicators.note: harvested is read as cut and gathered up, mixing the letters
last of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A friend brought in the grain and the end of the hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A crony is a close friend or companion, often a long-standing one.

clue.text: Beginning of a big build-up?

parts.note: build-up reads as hype or anticipation, but it is a literal construction

explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial block laid at the start of construction marks the beginning of a building.

clue.text: Communication one allows?

definitions.meaning: a written message sent by post
one who lets, a person who permits

explanation.definitionFit: A written note is a communication, and someone who lets is one who allows.

clue.text: Scan note before exercising the canines

parts.note: to eye something is to scan it
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: exercising suggests working the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: Look at a note before working out the dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' rearranges 'the' into ETH; 'canines' suggests dogs but means pointed teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye teeth are the canine teeth of the upper jaw, below the eyes.
